question: Describe a situation where you made an important business decision without consulting your manager. What was the situation and how did it turn out? Would you have done anything differently?

raiseTranscript.text: We had a customer-facing dashboard that was showing stale data for three days because of a config mismatch in the ETL job. My manager was out, so I decided to roll back the last config change myself after checking the logs and confirming it was the root cause. It restored the data within an hour.
What was the risk if you were wrong?
The dashboard would have stayed broken another day, but rollback was reversible in five minutes so I documented it in the runbook and pinged the on-call channel.
Would you do anything differently?
I would have added a short note in the team Slack before rolling back so others knew it was in progress.

raiseNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you made an important business decision without consulting your manager...
- Junior IC, fixed customer dashboard stale data by rolling back ETL config while manager OOO
- Verified root cause via logs, rollback took 5 min and was reversible
- Outcome: data restored in 1 hour, documented in runbook and notified on-call
Quote: "I would have added a short note in the team Slack before rolling back"
Follow-up: risk if wrong? "Dashboard stays broken another day but reversible"
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Bias for Action at junior level. The candidate owned a local production issue, verified the cause, executed a reversible fix, and documented the change. The story shows appropriate scope for 0-2 years experience and awareness of reversibility. The follow-up answer about adding a Slack note demonstrates coachability and learning. Biggest strength is the clear ownership of the outcome without overstepping into team-wide changes.

lowerTranscript.text: Our pricing page had a typo in the annual plan copy. I updated it live without telling anyone because it looked wrong and I didn't want to wait for the next sprint.
How did you know it was the right change?
It just seemed obvious. Sales never complained so I assumed it was fine.
Would you do anything differently?
Probably not, it was a small text change and no one noticed.

lowerNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you made an important business decision without consulting your manager...
- Changed pricing page copy live without approval or verification
- No data or stakeholder check; assumed "obvious"
- Outcome: no visible impact but no process followed
Quote: "It just seemed obvious. Sales never complained so I assumed it was fine."
Follow-up: would do differently? "Probably not"
junior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for Bias for Action at junior level. The candidate treated a visible but low-risk change as an individual decision without checking impact or involving the right owner. No evidence of verification or learning from the action. The follow-up shows limited reflection. Biggest gap is absence of any mechanism to confirm the change was correct before acting.

raiseTranscript.text: Two teams were blocked on a shared dependency that was deprioritized. I decided to pull the work into our sprint and deliver the integration layer ourselves after estimating it would take two weeks and unblock three downstream features.
How did you align the other teams?
I wrote a one-page proposal with the trade-off, shared it in the cross-team channel, and got explicit thumbs-up from both leads before starting.
Would you have done anything differently?
I would have surfaced the decision to my manager the same day rather than the next standup so she had visibility earlier.

raiseNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you made an important business decision without consulting your manager...
- Senior engineer, pulled shared dependency work into sprint to unblock two teams
- Two-week estimate, delivered integration layer, unblocked three features
- Aligned via one-page proposal and explicit cross-team thumbs-up
Quote: "I would have surfaced the decision to my manager the same day"
Follow-up: align others? "Wrote proposal and got explicit thumbs-up from both leads"
senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Bias for Action at senior level. The candidate identified a cross-team blocker, quantified the impact, created a lightweight alignment artifact, and executed without waiting for manager direction. The decision stayed within individual scope while delivering measurable downstream value. The follow-up shows appropriate escalation awareness. Biggest strength is the combination of speed and lightweight coordination without requiring authority.

lowerTranscript.text: I chose to rewrite a core service in a new language because the current one was hard to maintain. I started the spike on my own and told my manager two weeks later.
What was the business impact of the delay?
We missed a couple of feature deadlines but the new service will be better long term.
Would you have done anything differently?
I would have asked for a dedicated two-week hackathon instead of doing it in parallel.

lowerNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you made an important business decision without consulting your manager...
- Senior engineer, started full rewrite of core service without alignment
- Two-week parallel spike, missed feature deadlines
- No upfront trade-off or stakeholder check
Quote: "We missed a couple of feature deadlines but the new service will be better long term."
Follow-up: business impact? "Missed a couple of feature deadlines"
senior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for Bias for Action at senior level. The candidate initiated a high-risk architectural change without quantifying cost or securing cross-team buy-in. The outcome traded short-term delivery commitments for an unapproved long-term bet. The follow-up still frames the rewrite as the right direction rather than questioning the decision process. Biggest gap is lack of visible trade-off analysis before committing team capacity.

raiseTranscript.text: Our support queue was growing because the on-call rotation was understaffed after two people left. I approved hiring a contractor for 90 days and adjusted the rotation to include the new person without waiting for the quarterly headcount meeting.
How did you handle the budget?
I used unspent contractor budget from another project and got retroactive approval from finance the next week.
Would you have done anything differently?
I would have written a short memo to the leadership team the same day so they weren't surprised by the spend.

raiseNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you made an important business decision without consulting your manager...
- Manager, approved 90-day contractor to fix support queue after attrition
- Used existing unspent budget, adjusted rotation, reduced queue time
- Got retroactive finance approval
Quote: "I would have written a short memo to the leadership team the same day"
Follow-up: budget handling? "Used unspent contractor budget from another project"
manager.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Bias for Action at manager level. The candidate acted on a clear team-level pain point by reallocating existing budget and adjusting process, then secured retroactive approval. The decision directly improved a team outcome metric. The follow-up shows awareness of upward communication. Biggest strength is creating leverage for the team without waiting for perfect process.

lowerTranscript.text: I let the team skip the weekly planning meeting for two weeks so they could focus on a launch. I didn't tell my director until the launch slipped.
What signal told you the launch was at risk?
The team told me they were behind but I trusted them to catch up.
Would you have done anything differently?
I would have asked for a status update mid-week instead of waiting until the end.

lowerNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you made an important business decision without consulting your manager...
- Manager, canceled team planning meetings for two weeks without escalation
- Launch slipped, no early warning to director
- Relied on team self-report without verification
Quote: "I trusted them to catch up"
Follow-up: risk signal? "The team told me they were behind"
manager.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for Bias for Action at manager level. The candidate removed a core team process without visibility or contingency, then failed to escalate when delivery risk appeared. The outcome shows the decision created rather than reduced team risk. The follow-up still places responsibility on the team rather than the manager's choice to stay silent. Biggest gap is absence of any mechanism to monitor the impact of the decision.

raiseTranscript.text: We were losing enterprise deals because our SOC2 certification timeline was 18 months out. I authorized starting the audit with an external firm using unallocated G&A budget and set a six-month target, then informed the board at the next meeting.
What was the expected revenue impact?
We modeled $4M in pipeline that was blocked on the certification; the model showed we would recover the audit cost in the first two closed deals.
Would you have done anything differently?
I would have briefed the CFO the same afternoon rather than waiting for the weekly sync so she could adjust the cash forecast.

raiseNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you made an important business decision without consulting your manager...
- Exec, authorized early SOC2 audit using unallocated budget to unblock enterprise deals
- Six-month target vs 18-month plan, modeled $4M pipeline impact
- Informed board after the fact
Quote: "I would have briefed the CFO the same afternoon"
Follow-up: revenue impact? "$4M in pipeline that was blocked on the certification"
exec.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Bias for Action at exec level. The candidate identified a strategic blocker to revenue, used available budget to compress a long-cycle compliance item, and quantified the business case. The decision operated at org level with clear trade-off visibility. The follow-up reflects appropriate peer communication. Biggest strength is linking a single decision to measurable business outcome without requiring perfect consensus first.

lowerTranscript.text: I greenlit a new market expansion into Brazil because the TAM looked attractive. We spent nine months building local infrastructure before realizing regulatory requirements made the unit economics negative.
When did you first see the regulatory issue?
The legal team flagged it in month four but the team thought they could work around it.
Would you have done anything differently?
I would have required a formal legal sign-off before committing the first engineering headcount.

lowerNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you made an important business decision without consulting your manager...
- Exec, approved Brazil market expansion based on TAM
- Nine months and negative unit economics after regulatory discovery
- Legal flag at month four not escalated to decision point
Quote: "The legal team flagged it in month four but the team thought they could work around it"
Follow-up: when flagged? "Month four"
exec.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for Bias for Action at exec level. The candidate committed significant resources to a market entry without securing cross-functional sign-off on regulatory risk. The outcome required nine months to surface a fatal flaw that was known internally. The follow-up still treats the issue as a process fix rather than a decision-quality problem. Biggest gap is lack of early risk gating before large resource allocation.

diagnostic.junior: Local production fix or small process change
diagnostic.senior: Cross-team blocker with quantified downstream impact
diagnostic.manager: Team-level resource reallocation with budget awareness
diagnostic.exec: Org-level strategic blocker with revenue model

diagnostic.senior: One-page proposal with explicit cross-team thumbs-up
diagnostic.exec: Informed board after committing unallocated budget
Modeled $4M pipeline recovery vs audit cost

diagnostic.junior: Would add Slack note next time
diagnostic.senior: Would surface to manager same day
diagnostic.manager: Would write memo to leadership same day

diagnostic.senior: Next standup instead of same day
diagnostic.exec: Next board meeting instead of same day
